tier_reason: First-party QuestDB blog with a public harness (github.com/javier/questdb_qwp_egress_to_arrow_perf: read_bench_questdb.py, read_bench_clickhouse.py, bench.sh) and stated AWS instance types, but no CPU model, no compiler/JVM flags, and ClickHouse pinned only as the unversioned 'latest' Docker image; the post itself calls it 'not a benchmark... an informal test', so C, not A/B.

corrections.workload: Streaming the last 500 million rows of a byte-identical trades table (symbol, side, price, amount, timestamp) out of the database across a 100 Gbps network into Apache Arrow batches in a Python client process, with N parallel reader connections, comparing QuestDB's QWP WebSocket egress (QuestDB 10.0.x) against ClickHouse native TCP (clickhouse-driver execute) and Arrow-over-HTTP (clickhouse-connect query_arrow_stream), with TimescaleDB as a further reference; engines on default settings.
corrections.claimed_speedup: 1.55x faster than ClickHouse's fastest configuration of any kind (QuestDB ~220M rows/s at 8 readers vs ClickHouse native TCP 141.9M rows/s at 8 readers) and 2.35x faster than ClickHouse's fastest streaming configuration (Arrow over HTTP, 93.8M rows/s), on 500M rows; on the 2B-row run QuestDB peaked at 291.9M rows/s (12 readers) vs ClickHouse Arrow HTTP 173.8M and native 165.5M rows/s (16 readers), about 1.68x (derived from page data)
corrections.caveats: First-party QuestDB blog (Javier Ramirez); both the post and the harness README say it is 'not a benchmark' but an informal, directional test of the client egress path (Python client, engines on defaults), not an engine ranking. The harness is public but has no license file, pins questdb/questdb:10.0.0 while ClickHouse runs the unversioned clickhouse-server:latest image, and states no CPU model (only m8gn.8xlarge/c8gn.8xlarge instance types) or build flags, so it is capped at C. Separate corroboration: on ClickBench c7a.metal-48xl, QuestDB's hot-run total is 5.40s (2026-09-26 result) vs DuckDB's 15.70s (2026-05-11), but QuestDB is much slower on cold runs (502.2s vs 162.8s) and load (327s vs 98s). These figures are derived from the raw ClickBench JSON.

notes: The numbers match the blog exactly. The only field that was wrong was compared_against_cpp_std_directly: the baseline is ClickHouse, not a C++ std library. The ClickBench aside checks out for hot runs only, so I added the cold-run and load gaps to the caveats.

tier_reason: First-party, author-run comparison against DuckDB v1.4.3 with public code (bench/clickbench/official_bench.py plus the 43 verbatim ClickBench queries). No CPU model, compiler or flags are given, and the README itself calls the numbers anecdotal, so it is C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Current repo ClickBench-43 run vs DuckDB v1.4.3 (min of 3 runs, one local machine): SlothDB faster on 29 of 40 comparable queries, with a geomean DuckDB/SlothDB time ratio of 1.24x. The total min-of-3 wall time is SlothDB 71.1s vs DuckDB 65.2s, so SlothDB is slower in aggregate. 7 of 40 results differ from DuckDB's, and SlothDB times out on Q19, Q29 and Q33. An earlier HN post (2026-05-01) claimed '1.35X to 5X faster than DuckDB and Clickhouse' on the 14GB/100M-row hits.parquet; the README now calls all numbers anecdotal and query-shape-specific.
corrections.workload: Author-run ClickBench-43 (the DuckDB variant of the queries, verbatim) over hits_typed.parquet queried directly by both engines on the same local machine, compared with DuckDB v1.4.3 (3 trials, min reported, 120s timeout), via bench/clickbench/official_bench.py; plus a bench/run.py mixed suite. The earlier HN claim also named ClickHouse, but the repo has no ClickHouse numbers.
corrections.caveats: Self-disclosed low-confidence result: the README 'Status' and 'Performance' sections call the numbers anecdotal ('one workstation against one DuckDB version'). They say some wins come from a per-query handler dispatch rather than the general engine, and the project states no ClickBench vendor PR is planned while that dispatch remains. In the repo's own ClickBench-43 table SlothDB loses on total wall time (71.1s vs 65.2s), returns results that differ from DuckDB's on 7 queries (Q18's 14.81x 'win' among them), and times out on 3. The HN '5x' headline is not supported by any current repo data. No hardware, compiler or flags are stated. Tagged rather than excluded; confidence is low.

notes: The README no longer contains any benchmark numbers. The real data is bench/clickbench/official_results.md (last changed 2026-05-19), and it shows only a modest geomean 1.24x win with correctness diffs and an aggregate loss, so I rewrote claimed_speedup. I confirmed the HN 1.35x-5x claim via HN Algolia (item 47971921). Metadata checks out: MIT, 413 stars, last commit 2026-06-03, active.

tier_reason: The peer-reviewed CIDR 2021 paper states the ratios verbatim along with gcc/g++ 9.3.0 and a Xeon Platinum 8124M CPU. However, it gives no optimization flags and publishes no benchmark-suite code (it only says it borrowed from SOSD), and it measured the author's own C implementation, not this repo. So it is B, not A.

corrections.stars_or_usage: 9 stars; this C++ implementation is the CHT component of PLEX (Stoian et al., 'Towards Practical Learned Indexing', AIDB 2021)
corrections.caveats: The numbers come from the CIDR 2021 paper (Andrew Crotty, 'Hist-Tree: Those Who Ignore It Are Doomed to Learn'). That paper benchmarks Crotty's own C implementation with a C++ suite borrowed from SOSD and publishes neither. This repo is a separate C++ reimplementation of the compact Hist-Tree by Mihail Stoian (MIT, 2021). The paper's speedups were therefore not measured on this code, and the paper states no optimization flags. The PLEX paper notes this implementation does not support duplicate keys, so it could not run SOSD's wiki dataset. The repo's bench.cc is only a parameter grid search on synthetic data with no baseline. There is no README benchmark section, and there have been no commits since 2021-07-17.

notes: All claimed ratios appear verbatim in the paper: RMI 1.1-1.8x, PGM 1.7-2.5x, RS 1.2-2.7x, CHT 2-3x over HT, build time more than 3.7x/19x faster than RMI on face/wiki. It is downgraded from A to B because the paper has no public benchmark code or flags and measured a different implementation. Metadata checks out: MIT, 9 stars, last commit 2021-07-17, abandoned.
